title: Capstone evaluation and revision
goals: Run a frozen final evaluation with complete accounting
Separate error analysis from an untouched-test claim
Document revisions and their evidence status

prerequisite.prompt: What changes after final-test labels inform a revision?
prerequisite.answer: The inspected set becomes development evidence for the revised version.

vocabulary: Assessment of the frozen procedure on held-out evidence
A documented inspection of mistakes and missing predictions
A record of changes, reasons and affected evidence
Whether a result is development, untouched test or post-test reuse

blocks.text: The teacher releases final-test labels only after checking the freeze record. Score baseline and candidate on the same planned rows. Save every prediction, denominator and failure. Do not edit a model while reading labels and then present only the edited version as the original test.

Use fictional classroom data throughout this investigation. Keep the task, units, reference labels and data split visible as you reason. Earlier weeks supplied the model-building process; this week examines capstone evaluation and revision.

Illustrative frozen test has 12 rows: candidate[[7, 1],[2, 2]], baseline[[8, 0],[4, 0]], blocked positive. Candidate accuracy 9/12=75 percent, precision 2/3 and recall 2/4; baseline accuracy 8/12 about 66.7 percent. The candidate adds one false alarm and misses two rather than four blocked cases.

Before continuing, underline the decision rule and circle the evidence that supports the conclusion. Explain the example to a partner without replacing the counts or conditions with a stronger claim. Keep the distinction between an observed result and a proposed next step.

blocks.title: Capstone evaluation and revision at a glance
blocks.caption: Compare the result with validation without claiming they should be identical. Check error types and coverage. A one-case accuracy difference on twelve rows supports a cautious classroom comparison, not a general reliability guarantee. Keep the original prediction ledger unchanged.

blocks.label: What does the one-correct-case improvement establish? Explain the steps or evidence behind your response.

blocks.text: If dim examples account for both misses, record that observation and inspect collection conditions. It is a hypothesis for investigation, not proof that lighting caused the failures. A proposed feature or model change creates version 2. Scores on the same inspected test must be labelled post-test development.

Submit the frozen test report, error audit, revision proposal and updated model card. A revision proposal may conclude that more appropriate data or a simpler baseline is preferable. If no fresh test is available, stop at a transparent proposal instead of claiming the revision has been independently validated.

blocks.label: What must remain visible when version 2 is proposed without a fresh test?

workbook.title: Score the frozen test
workbook.prompt: Compute the worked candidate metrics and baseline accuracy.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Candidate accuracy 9/12=75 percent, precision 2/3, recall 2/4; baseline 8/12 about 66.7 percent, with all four blocked cases missed.

workbook.title: Audit a difference
workbook.prompt: What does the one-correct-case improvement establish?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: It establishes a difference on these 12 examples under the saved procedure, not reliable improvement for every future population.

workbook.title: Label a revision
workbook.prompt: A threshold changes after test errors are read. Label its score on the same rows.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Post-test development or reused-test evidence for the revised version, not an untouched final test.

workbook.title: Apply independently
workbook.prompt: Frozen candidate[[6, 2],[1, 3]] and baseline[[8, 0],[4, 0]] on 12 cases. Compute candidate metrics and compare error types.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Candidate accuracy 9/12=75 percent, precision 3/5=60 percent, recall 3/4=75 percent. Baseline FP 0 FN 4 versus candidate FP 2 FN 1; baseline accuracy 8/12.

workbook.title: Update the card
workbook.prompt: What must remain visible when version 2 is proposed without a fresh test?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Version 1 frozen results, reason for change, reused-evidence status and the fact that version 2 has no new independent final evaluation.

teacher.background: Teach two 45-minute sessions. This week focuses on capstone evaluation and revision. Model the worked example first, collect the new W 4 case independently before feedback, and use the fresh retry to check transfer. Award credit for traceable reasoning and bounded claims, including justified uncertainty.
materials: Paper, pencils and a calculator for fractions
The fictional examples and a blank evidence table
Saved classroom project records for critique; no personal student dataset required
sessions: Use the prerequisite question: What changes after final-test labels inform a revision? Check the explanation before proceeding.
Verify each team freeze record before releasing final labels. Review the worked example and separate illustrative numbers from actual project evidence.
Teams run or trace frozen baseline and candidate predictions on all planned test cases. Save the unchanged prediction ledger and account for failures.
Teams calculate metrics and inspect error types. Use W1–W3 to check calculations and evidence status before writing claims.
Retrieve the distinction between final evaluation and error audit. Invite a counterexample to an overconfident claim.
Teams write an error audit and propose one follow-up tied to an observed limit. Keep version1 results unchanged.
Collect W4 independently. Teams then update their model card and clearly mark any revision as untested or supported only by reused development evidence.
Use W 5 and the exit response to assess limits. Give targeted feedback, then the fresh retry. Save evidence of independent understanding.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided response: It establishes a difference on these 12 examples under the saved procedure, not reliable improvement for every future population. Exit response: Version 1 frozen results, reason for change, reused-evidence status and the fact that version 2 has no new independent final evaluation.
misconceptions: Ask for the relevant counts, units, procedure or saved record. For this week: Candidate accuracy 9/12=75 percent, precision 2/3, recall 2/4; baseline 8/12 about 66.7 percent, with all four blocked cases missed.
A stronger claim makes a stronger project
Version 1 frozen results, reason for change, reused-evidence status and the fact that version 2 has no new independent final evaluation.
The new case can be copied from the example

The independent task changes the evidence. Require a fresh explanation: Candidate accuracy 9/12=75 percent, precision 3/5=60 percent, recall 3/4=75 percent. Baseline FP 0 FN 4 versus candidate FP 2 FN 1; baseline accuracy 8/12.
teacher.assessment: For independent W 4, require: Candidate accuracy 9/12=75 percent, precision 3/5=60 percent, recall 3/4=75 percent. Baseline FP 0 FN 4 versus candidate FP 2 FN 1; baseline accuracy 8/12. Fresh retry candidate[[5, 1],[2, 2]] on 10 cases: accuracy 7/10, precision 2/3, recall 2/4. Require a test-status statement before any proposed tuning. Mark each criterion as independent, supported or not yet demonstrated. Reassess the reasoning after feedback; do not replace the first attempt silently.
teacher.support: Provide a blank evidence table and allow a verbal explanation before writing. Highlight the given conditions without supplying the W 4 conclusion. Use final evaluation and error audit in full sentences. Extension: alter one condition in the worked example and explain which conclusion changes and which remains supported.
teacher.next: Next week: Machine learning project defense. Carry forward the saved evidence and the distinction between development choices and justified claims.
